cards.title: A ship with a purpose
cards.idea: In 1600, English merchants got a royal charter to trade in the East. Their ships carried empty holds out and Indian goods back.

interaction.prompt: Tap the item the ships came to India to collect

cards.reveal: They wanted spices, cotton cloth, silk and indigo. India's goods sold for high prices in Europe, so trade meant huge profit.

cards.title: Not just a shop
cards.idea: To store goods safely, the Company built fortified warehouses called factories at ports like Surat, Madras and Calcutta.

interaction.prompt: Tap the coastal spot where a factory would be built

cards.reveal: Factories sat on the coast for easy loading. Walls and guards protected goods, but slowly these forts also held soldiers.

cards.title: Trade turns to power
cards.idea: Rival European companies competed too. To protect trade, the Company kept its own army and began interfering in local politics.

interaction.prompt: Drag the label to what a trading company was not supposed to have

cards.reveal: An army. A trading firm now had cannons and soldiers, letting it pressure Indian rulers and control the terms of trade.

cards.title: Naming the shift
cards.idea: The English East India Company began as traders under a 1600 charter, then used forts and armies to gain political control.

interaction.prompt: Type the year the Company received its royal charter

cards.reveal: 1600. Queen Elizabeth I's charter gave a monopoly on eastern trade. From this trading start grew nearly two centuries of British rule.

cards.title: The turning point
cards.idea: At the Battle of Plassey in 1757, the Company defeated Bengal's Nawab, gaining real land control for the first time.

interaction.prompt: Tap the region the Company controlled after Plassey

cards.reveal: Bengal. Winning here gave the Company revenue and territory. Trade had become empire, funded by taxes from Indian land.

workbook.prompt: Why did the English East India Company first come to India?
options: To trade in goods like spices and cloth
workbook.answer: To trade in goods like spices and cloth

workbook.prompt: The fortified warehouses the Company built at ports were called ________.
What did the Company have that an ordinary trading firm would not?

boss.prompt: How did the Company change from a trader into a ruler?
options: It used forts and armies to gain political control
It bought all of India in one payment
It stopped trading completely from the start
boss.answer: It used forts and armies to gain political control

boss.prompt: After the Battle of ________ in 1757, the Company gained control of Bengal.
Why was controlling Bengal so important to the Company?
options: It gave them revenue and territory to fund power
It had the only port in India
It ended all European rivals instantly
boss.answer: It gave them revenue and territory to fund power
